entries.label: M-01
entries.title: _skimSurplus over-skim via duplicate clients[] under-backs principal

fixEvidence.summary: story-041 removed the caller-supplied clients[] list (skim is now the no-list skimSurplus(token,recipient) over an owner-managed EnumerableSet _authorizedClients, so duplicates cannot be injected and the set is distinct by construction), and added a loud aggregate-surplus ceiling at ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol#L434: require(totalShares <= vault.convertToShares(totalValue - totalDeposited), 'ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy: skim exceeds aggregate surplus'). The duplicate-driven over-skim is structurally unconstructible and arithmetically bounded: Sigma floor(convertToShares(surplus_i)) <= floor(convertToShares(Sigma surplus_i)) <= floor(k * aggregateSurplus) -- no spurious revert, no principal breach (convergent code-scanner + econ-scanner verdict).

entries.label: M-02
entries.title: NAV-anchored minOut is execution-price-blind, enabling sandwich value leak
entries.reconfirmedNote: Reconfirmed OPEN at phoenix-vault-06 (043ff2c) via duplicates this run (PATTERN-001/002). story-041's single-aggregate-swap rewrite did not change the root cause: minOut is still derived from NAV (convertToAssets) rather than execution price, leaving the swap sandwich-exploitable.
entries.triageNote: Accepted by design (route: sUSDe/USDe). The strategy anchors swap minOut to ERC4626 NAV (convertToShares/convertToAssets) rather than an oracle or signed price, a deliberate trust-minimization choice. Review confirmed there is no oracle-free, single-transaction way to detect a skewed pool — the obvious get_dy execution-time cross-check is circular (it reads the reserves an attacker would have just skewed) — so the alternatives (oracle distortion, signer compromise) trade a bounded, quantifiable leak for unbounded trust assumptions. We accept the residual. Residual risk (retained, bounded): up to slippageToleranceBps × tradeSize per swap; economically marginal on the deep sUSDe/USDe pair at normal trade-size-to-depth, growing with looser tolerance, thinner pools, depeg windows, or large swaps relative to depth; bounded because sUSDe NAV is not atomically manipulable (cannot escalate to theft on this route). Compensating control to carry upstream: slippageToleranceBps has no upper bound and defaults to 0 — add a require-enforced hard ceiling + sane nonzero default; operationally keep tolerance near organic slippage and consider private orderflow for large rebalances. Forward-looking: do not deploy this strategy over an ERC4626 whose share price is atomically manipulable — there the NAV reference becomes attacker-controlled and the same code path is a High-severity theft primitive. The merged ex-M-03 last-withdrawer amplification does not apply: clients are owner-curated (setClient onlyOwner), not mutually-distrusting; the requested-not-received decrement is documented-intentional protocol-owned yield. Triaged 2026-05-27.

entries.label: M-03
entries.title: Requested-not-received decrement socialises slippage, causing last-withdrawer shortfall
entries.note: No standalone loss primitive; amplifies M-02's slippage leak by concentrating the share-backing deficit onto the last withdrawer via the requested-not-received decrement. Confirmed by poc-validation.md counterfactual (fair deposits + adverse withdrawals only -> no concentrated shortfall). Fingerprint retained so a future standalone recurrence can still be matched.

entries.label: L-01
entries.title: slippageToleranceBps default-0 plus setter missing sane cap (missing validation)
entries.reconfirmedNote: Reconfirmed OPEN at phoenix-vault-06 (043ff2c) via PATTERN-001 (bps-half). setSlippageTolerance still accepts an unbounded bps value and defaults to 0; root cause unchanged by the skim rewrite.

entries.label: L-02
entries.title: skimSurplus unbounded iteration over owner-grown authorized-client set (no pagination)
entries.restatedNote: RESTATED/NARROWED at phoenix-vault-06 (043ff2c). Original entry had two sub-vectors. (1) ZERO-ADDRESS WHOLE-BATCH REVERT -- RESOLVED by story-041: the caller no longer supplies the client list; setClient rejects the zero address so it can never enter the set, and the in-loop zero-address check (ERC4626MarketYieldStrategy.sol#L421) is now unreachable defense-in-depth. (2) UNBOUNDED LOOP -- PERSISTS, transformed: skimSurplus now iterates the full owner-managed _authorizedClients EnumerableSet with no pagination (all-or-nothing). This is owner-controlled growth -- an admin would have to authorize an extreme number of clients to brick the skim -- so it remains an owner-bounded availability/gas note at Low. PATTERN-006 and SLITHER-005 (calls-loop) consolidate INTO this entry; no separate entries were created.
entries.note: This is almost certainly unlikely to become an issue as we're likely to never have more than 3 clients.

entries.label: C-01
entries.title: Centralization / owner-power bundle
entries.reconfirmedNote: Reconfirmed OPEN at phoenix-vault-06 (043ff2c) via PATTERN-005. story-041 ADDS owner power: an owner-managed authorized-client EnumerableSet (setClient), and the rewritten skim sends 100% of aggregate surplus to a single withdrawer-chosen recipient (trusted-actor discretion). The single-aggregate-swap rewrite did not change the centralization root cause.
